background: The Toronto-Dominion Bank is Canada's second-largest bank, funded by Canadian and US deposits and lending on Canadian mortgages and to businesses, with a large US retail bank along the east coast that has been under a regulatory asset cap after its anti-money-laundering failures.
synthesis: The bank is rated A+ on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at A, all three on a stable outlook, with the last move a one-notch downgrade by one of the three on 23 Oct 2024, which followed the US enforcement action. Capital is strong against Canadian peers, with CET1 of 14.3% in the top quarter, though it has fallen 0.6 points since 30 Apr 2025, and no leverage or liquidity figures are held here. The newest flagged item, on 7 Sep 2026, is a senior executive's departure after less than a year in the job, while the earlier items are mostly good, with quarterly profit up strongly. Well capitalised, with the US remediation the thing to watch.
